React · Core concepts

Why should we avoid using array indexes as keys?

Answer

If the list can be reordered, filtered, or have items inserted/removed, index keys break identity: the item at index 0 is now a different item but has the same key.

Consequences:

  • Wrong component state sticks to the wrong row (e.g. a checked checkbox or typed input "jumps" to another item).
  • Unnecessary re-renders / DOM updates for every item after the change.

Index keys are acceptable only when the list is static (never reordered/filtered) and items have no state. Otherwise use a stable unique id (or generate one when data is created, not during render).
